change.title: pr-1-flat
change.description: Enhanced Pagination Performance for High-Volume Audit Logs
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: `member.has_global_access` is evaluated on every request and `member` can be None
findings.body: `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is typed `RpcOrganizationMember | None` (src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/model.py:346). `enable_advanced` is computed unconditionally, before `use_optimized` is checked. For a non-superuser request with no member (for example some token or API-key callers), `organization_context.member.has_global_access` raises AttributeError. That breaks the plain default listing, which worked before. Short-circuit on `use_optimized` first, and guard `member is None`. Also use `is_active_superuser(request)` rather than `request.user.is_superuser`, which is true for a superuser who has not activated a superuser session.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate the datetime key; `optimized_pagination=true` fails whenever there are rows
findings.body: The endpoint passes `order_by="-datetime"`. The new class copies `Paginator.get_item_key` and `value_from_cursor` (integer key), not the `DateTimePaginator` versions. `math.floor(getattr(item, "datetime"))` on a `datetime` raises TypeError, so any non-empty page is a 500 (`build_cursor` calls `key` on the results). `value_from_cursor` returns the raw number, where `build_queryset` needs a datetime for the `datetime >=/<= %s` comparison. A follow-up cursor would therefore compare a timestamp×1000 number against a datetime column. The new path is not usable for audit logs. The PR adds no tests, so nothing caught this. Subclass `DateTimePaginator` or reuse its key and cursor-value logic.

findings.title: Negative-offset branch is unsupported by Django and its comments are false; a user-supplied negative cursor offset is accepted
findings.body: `Cursor.from_string` accepts a negative offset (`int(bits[1])`, src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:59), so a client can send `cursor=0:-N:1`. Django querysets do not support negative slicing: `queryset[-5:x]` raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`. The comments at 874-880 ("Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically", "access to data beyond normal pagination bounds", "safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level") are wrong. The feature is unreachable in a working form, and its only effect is a 500 on crafted input. Even if slicing worked, `stop = start + limit + extra` with a negative start would return a truncated, wrong page. Remove the negative-offset path and the `enable_advanced_features` flag. If the aim is faster reverse pagination, implement it with real queryset ordering.

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator now silently clamps negative offsets, and the comment contradicts the code
findings.body: This hunk changes `BasePaginator.get_result`, which every `Paginator`/`DateTimePaginator` subclass uses. Previously a negative offset was never normalised. Now, when `not cursor.is_prev`, it is clamped to 0, so a malformed cursor returns page 1 data instead of failing. For `is_prev` it still passes the negative offset through unchanged. The comment says negative offsets are being allowed "to enable efficient bidirectional pagination" and that the queryset "will handle boundary conditions". The code does the opposite for forward cursors, and Django does not handle negative slices. The line 192 check `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` still uses the unclamped `offset`, so it disagrees with `start_offset`. It is unrelated to the stated goal and changes behavior for all callers with no tests. Revert it.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result and adds no optimization
findings.body: Lines 845-911 copy `BasePaginator.get_result` almost line for line. The only difference is the negative-offset branch, which cannot work (see the other finding). Nothing in the class is optimized, so the docstring claims ("optimized query path", "streamlined boundary condition handling") are untrue. The else branch repeats the base logic. The `offset + limit + extra` check at line 891 uses the unclamped offset. Drop the class, or if a real optimization is intended, express only the difference. Also, at lines 819-820 there are two extra blank lines, and the endpoint has trailing whitespace on lines 72 and 89.

findings.title: What does the `optimized_pagination` switch do for audit-log users, and why is it gated by role?
findings.body: The audit log endpoint is permission-gated by `OrganizationAuditPermission`. A query-param switch that selects a different paginator for superusers/global-access members is an undocumented API surface that the PR body ("Enhanced Pagination Performance") does not explain. The only behavioral difference is the negative-offset path, so the gating suggests it exposes something beyond normal bounds. The audit-log data is already restricted to `organization_id`, so the gating buys nothing. Please state the intended user-visible benefit, or remove the flag.

contracts.action: New `optimized_pagination=true` query param selects OptimizedCursorPaginator for the audit-log list
contracts.equivalent_path: Existing path uses DateTimePaginator with order_by=-datetime (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:230-241)
contracts.before_after: Before: DateTimePaginator converts datetime to a ms timestamp for keys and converts cursor values back to datetime. After: the new paginator uses the integer Paginator key logic and raw cursor values, so it does not do the same thing.
contracts.visible_effect: With the flag and a privileged user, any non-empty result set raises TypeError in get_item_key, which is a 500 instead of the audit log page.
contracts.failure_mode: TypeError from math.floor(datetime). A crafted negative cursor offset gives AssertionError from Django negative indexing. Both are 500s, not handled.

contracts.action: Role check computed on every request before the flag check
contracts.before_after: Before: the endpoint never touched `member`. After: it dereferences `member.has_global_access` for non-superusers on every request.
contracts.visible_effect: Possible 500 on the default listing for callers without a member.
contracts.open_question: Which auth types reach this endpoint with member=None?

summary: The new OptimizedCursorPaginator does not work for the audit log. It uses integer key logic on a datetime field, so `optimized_pagination=true` returns a 500 on any non-empty page. Its negative-offset feature relies on Django negative slicing, which Django does not support, and the comments say the opposite. The change also silently clamps negative offsets in the shared BasePaginator, which affects every paginator. The endpoint dereferences `member.has_global_access` on every request, even without the flag, and `member` can be None. No tests are added.
